# Follow-up review of final integrity fixes

Review only committed range `e4814ef939f7596316aab6c44cf3e12d2f112316..ece0c43eeaa80b9d385176f151ff52354ba3e8e8` read-only. Start from the settled findings in the previous round: plain templates/backtick strings misclassified as tagged templates, member expressions on allocated literals over-exempted, trailing-comma expect calls skipped, and combined pytest/pytest.mark wildcard imports overwriting each other.

The fixes use masked code for tag detection, require whole object/array literals for identity exemption, filter empty trailing argument spans, and resolve runtime suppression names across all wildcard import sources. Regressions failed before and pass after; all three isolated contract candidates and all 472 repository script tests pass.

Check each fix and look beyond it for introduced defects. In particular check tagged versus plain templates, whole-literal delimiter matching, empty-argument behavior, wildcard resolution order, and baseline subtraction. Do not re-report the tracked ledger correction or GitHub enforcement. Return at most three findings, or an empty findings list promptly.

summary: Reviewed the four integrity fixes: masked-code tagged-template detection, whole-literal identity exemption, empty trailing-argument filtering, and multi-source wildcard import resolution. Tagged-vs-plain templates, trailing commas, wildcard order, and baseline subtraction all behave correctly in isolation, and empty string literals are correctly retained (their masked spans normalize to '\"\"', not empty). One low-severity false positive remains in the whole-literal delimiter matching.

findings.title: Type-asserted object/array literals misclassified as self-comparisons
findings.trigger: An identity matcher over two identical literals carrying a TypeScript type suffix, e.g. assert.strictEqual([1] as const, [1] as const) or assert.strictEqual({a:1} satisfies Foo, {a:1} satisfies Foo) (also [1]! with a non-null assertion).
findings.consequence: The gate emits a V5 'new constant or self-comparing assertion' violation even though the operands are two freshly allocated objects/arrays compared by reference, so the assertion always fails at runtime and is not a tautology. This is a false positive that fails the integrity check for code it should exempt, and the classification message is misleading.
findings.evidence: self_comparing() at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:294-297 exempts an operand only when matching_delimiter(source.code, start, opening, ...) == end - 1; when 'as const', 'satisfies Foo', or '!' follows the closing delimiter, the delimiter is no longer the last character, so the exemption is skipped and the operand is reported as self-comparing. Verified via scan_typescript: both 'assert.strictEqual([1] as const, [1] as const)' and 'assert.strictEqual({a:1} satisfies Foo, {a:1} satisfies Foo)' produce a V5 marker.
